title: Just three basic mechanisms account for randomness

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Just three basic mechanisms account for randomness

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Apparent randomness in any system arises from one of just three basic mechanisms: continual random input from the environment, randomness transcribed from initial conditions, or intrinsic generation of randomness by the system's own rules with no random input.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But from my investigations of simple programs I have come to the conclusion that one can in fact identify just three basic mechanisms for randomness, as illustrated in the pictures below.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “Three Mechanisms for Randomness” (from p. 299), p. 299. Scope: all systems, natural or computational, that show apparent randomness

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Mechanism attribution is possible for controlled, well-instrumented cases. The exhaustive trichotomy over every system is partly conceptual and cannot be discriminated because classifications shift with boundary and observability.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a defined sample of stochastic-looking systems, fit causal models partitioning output uncertainty into environmental innovations, uncertain initial state, and deterministic amplification by internal dynamics. Test whether residual mechanisms are needed to explain predictive distributions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No dataset covers all systems.

The three categories overlap under different system boundaries.

Latent environmental inputs are indistinguishable from intrinsic dynamics.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.42
discriminating power: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: External noise, transcribed initial conditions, and no random input are a logical trichotomy about where randomness enters a model. Any system can be placed in one bin once that modeling choice is made, so the census cannot come out against the sentence. The pictures illustrate the bins; they do not test whether the bins are exhaustive.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sort systems by whether randomness is inserted at every step, only in the initial condition, or not at all. Every system falls in one of those three bins by construction, so the partition does not state an additional outcome that could fail.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The three mechanisms partition systems by where randomness is inserted.

No observation distinguishes this partition from itself restated in other words.
